page: Microsoft Azure E20_v4 is a memory-optimized virtual machine belonging to the Ev4 server family. It is built on the x86_64 architecture and powered by a dedicated Intel Xeon 8272CL processor running at 2.6 GHz. The configuration features 20 virtual CPUs, which correspond to 10 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled at 2.0 threads per core. The system is provisioned with 160.0 GB of RAM, yielding a high memory-to-vCPU ratio of 8.0 GB per vCPU. It operates under the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. This instance does not include local storage or bundled GPUs, and it offers zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Performance benchmarks place the E20_v4 consistently in the average tier across most compute and memory metrics. The single-core and multi-core stress-ng CPU benchmarks scored 1412.69 and 18613.51 respectively, while the Geekbench multi-core score reached 8313.0. Memory bandwidth tests show a read-only small block cached speed of 1034.46 GB/sec, dropping to 88.48 GB/sec for large uncached blocks, and a write speed of 43.27 GB/sec. Tradeoffs are evident in single-threaded compression and decompression tasks; gzip compression at 23.81 GB/sec and bzip3 decompression at 8.63 GB/sec both registered in the weak category. However, multi-threaded bzip3 decompression recovered to an average rating at 66.24 GB/sec.

Given its high memory density of 160.0 GB relative to its 20 vCPUs, the E20_v4 is qualitatively cost-efficient for memory-bound workloads that do not require local NVMe storage or GPU acceleration. It is configured for database operations, as demonstrated by its average Passmark database score of 7170.89 and a Redis SET throughput of 16.52 million operations per second. Other appropriate workloads include static web serving, software compilation, and small-scale language model inference, where it achieves 96.24 tokens per second for text generation on a 135M parameter model.
